finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test sends a server-side axios POST to an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL with no scheme, host, or IP validation. An attacker can reach internal services, loopback, or cloud metadata endpoints. The response status code is returned, which gives a port and host scan oracle and a blind SSRF primitive. Redirects are followed by axios by default.

trace.note: `pub` router created with no auth middleware; only `admin` gets requireAdmin (line 12)
upstream status returned to the caller via res.json

finding.guards_checked: No auth guard on the pub router. No URL parsing, scheme allowlist, private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking, DNS pinning, or redirect restriction. The only file in the repo is routes.js, so there is no other middleware to check. The mount point is not visible, but the router is exported as `pub` with no guard. The admin-only twin at routes.js:15 (/diagnostics/fetch) was not reported because requireAdmin gates it (checked at routes.js:7-12).

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 passes req.body.callback straight into axios.post with no validation and returns r.status. The `pub` router (routes.js:4) has no auth middleware, since only `admin` uses requireAdmin (routes.js:12). The mount point is not in the repo, so an upstream auth layer is possible but unseen.
